sq.q: \(\text{A rod of length 20 cm has its ends kept at } 0^\circ\text{C} \text{ and } 100^\circ\text{C} \text{ until steady state. Then the temperatures at the ends are interchanged. Find the temperature } u(x,t) \text{ after the change.}\)
answer: \(\text{Let } u(x,t)=u_1(x)+u_2(x,t), \text{ where } u_2 \text{ satisfies heat equation with } u_2(0,t)=0, u_2(20,t)=0.\)
\(\text{Solve for } u_2: u_2(x,t)=\sum_{n=1}^\infty B_n \sin\left(\frac{n\pi x}{20}\right) e^{-\alpha^2 n^2\pi^2 t/400}.\)

sq.q: \(\text{A string of length } \pi \text{ is fixed at both ends. It is initially displaced into the shape } y(x,0) = \begin{cases} x, & 0 \leq x \leq \pi/2 \\ \pi - x, & \pi/2 \leq x \leq \pi \end{cases} \text{ and released from rest. Find the displacement } y(x,t).\)
answer: \(\text{Wave equation: } \frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial t^2} = c^2 \frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial x^2}.\)
\(\text{Fourier sine coefficients: } B_n = \frac{2}{\pi} \left[ \int_0^{\pi/2} x \sin(nx) dx + \int_{\pi/2}^\pi (\pi-x) \sin(nx) dx \right].\)

lq.q: \(\text{A rod of length $l$ with insulated sides has ends kept at temperatures $0^\circ$ C and $100^\circ$C until steady state.}\\ \text{Then both ends are suddenly insulated. Find the temperature distribution.}\)
answer: Step Marks \(\text{Initial steady state: \(u_s(x)= \dfrac{100}{l}x.\)}\) (2 Marks) \(\text{After ends insulated: BCs become \(u_x(0,t)=0\), \(u_x(l,t)=0\) (no heat flow).}\) (2 Marks) \(\text{General solution for insulated ends: \(u(x,t)= A_0 + \sum A_n \cos\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right) e^{-\alpha^2 n^2\pi^2 t / l^2}.\)}\) (3 Marks) \(\text{Initial condition: \(u(x,0)= \dfrac{100}{l}x = A_0 + \sum A_n \cos\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right).\)}\) (2 Marks) \(\text{Compute \(A_0 = \dfrac{1}{l} \int_0^l \dfrac{100}{l}x dx = \dfrac{100}{l^2} \cdot \dfrac{l^2}{2} = 50.\)}\) (2 Marks) \(\text{\(A_n = \dfrac{2}{l} \int_0^l \dfrac{100}{l}x \cos\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right) dx\) for \(n\geq1.\)}\) (2 Marks) \(\text{Evaluate: \(A_n = \dfrac{200}{l^2} \int_0^l x \cos\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right) dx = \dfrac{200}{l^2} \left[ \dfrac{l^2}{n^2\pi^2} (\cos(n\pi)-1) \right] = \dfrac{200}{n^2\pi^2} ( (-1)^n - 1 ).\)}\) (3 Marks) \(\text{Thus \(u(x,t)= 50 + \sum\limits_{n=1}^{\infty} \dfrac{200}{n^2\pi^2}((-1)^n -1) \cos\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right) e^{-\alpha^2 n^2\pi^2 t / l^2}.\)}\) (1 Mark)
